$comment: The in-repo record of which CI checks can stop a merge to `main`, and why
the rest cannot (#542). Ruleset 16189198 carried no `required_status_checks`
rule at all, so every check was advisory: PR #540 merged while markdownlint
was reporting FAILURE and `main` went red until #541.
This file is the source of truth a human can read; the GitHub ruleset is the
copy that enforces it. `ts/test/workflow-false-green.test.ts` keeps the two
honest against the workflows: every `required` check must be produced by a
workflow that runs unconditionally on `pull_request` (a required check behind
a `paths:` filter never reports, and the PR can never merge), and every
check-producing job must appear here as either required or advisory with a
stated reason. A new job that is neither fails the suite rather than joining
the advisory pile by default.
ADR 0010: a check is promoted once its precision is known. That is a real
reason to wait. `nobody configured it` is not, and is what #542 was filed
about.
To apply this file to the ruleset:
gh api -X PUT repos/bop-clocktower/canary/rulesets/16189198 --input <payload>
See docs/knowledge/decisions/0011-required-status-checks.md for the procedure.
#678 — the confirmed reason a PR-time check can pass while the identical
commit fails post-merge. Read against the live ruleset with:
gh api repos/bop-clocktower/canary/rulesets/16189198
`strict` is GitHub's `strict_required_status_checks_policy`. With it
FALSE a PR merges without being up to date with `main`. Combined with the
default `actions/checkout` behaviour on `pull_request` — which checks out
the merge commit GitHub computed for that event, i.e. head merged into
`main` as of the last push to the PR BRANCH — a green check is a verdict
about `merge(head, main@t0)`. Nothing re-runs when the base moves to t1,
because base movement fires no check run on the PR. So the PR-time green
and the post-merge red are answers to two different questions, and the
gate is reporting after the fact rather than gating. #660 is the worked
example: its own `harness` check passed, the same commit failed
`check-arch` on `main`, and #663 inherited the failure and read as its
cause.
Recorded rather than silently flipped: setting `strict` to true forces
every open PR to update its branch whenever `main` moves, which is a real
cost to concurrent work and a maintainer's call, not a drive-by. The
field exists so the state is reviewable in the repo instead of living
only in a ruleset nobody reads.
The mitigation that IS in place: every workflow producing a required
check also runs on `push: main`, so a stale PR-time green is caught on
`main` within one run rather than surfacing as the NEXT PR's failure.
`guardian.yml` is the sole exemption — it reviews a pull-request diff
and has nothing to say about a push.

required.check: Code fences open and close correctly

$comment: Despite the workflow's display name — Architecture Enforcer — this job
does NOT run the architecture ratchet (#678). It runs `harness
check-deps` and `harness validate`; neither reads
`.harness/arch/baselines.json`. The ratchet lives in the `harness`
check above, via `harness ci check` plus the `check-arch` detail report
that `scripts/arch-verdict.mjs` classifies. That is why this job can be
green while a local `harness check-arch` exits 1: they are different
commands, not one gate disagreeing with itself.

advisory.reason: Precision not yet known (ADR 0010). The dogfood jobs run canary against canary and currently report a 409-finding baseline that #544 has not triaged. Promoting before the triage would block every PR on findings nobody has confirmed are real.
Same dogfood baseline as above (#544). Also exercises a packed npm install, which depends on registry availability — a network flake would read as a code failure.
Same dogfood baseline as above (#544). Promote alongside the other dogfood jobs once the baseline is triaged rather than one at a time.
Reports on accumulated run history, so its verdict depends on prior runs rather than on this PR's diff. A required check must be a function of the change under review.
Advisory by design — canary-katana records deleted and skipped tests and alarms only when the deletion removes the last coverage of a high-risk symbol. Same dogfood baseline (#544).

Not a gate. Triggers only on `pull_request: types: [labeled]` — an on-demand action a maintainer invokes to refresh the architecture baseline. It does not report on an ordinary PR, so requiring it would deadlock every PR that is never labeled.

reviews.reason: Deliberate, not a default (#542 step 4). Single-maintainer repo: raising this to 1 would mean self-approving every PR, which trains the reflex the gate exists to prevent. Revisit when a second maintainer joins.
